findings.summary: No test feeds the artifact list an entry with a missing or boolean repository id, so the type guards in the main-and-this-repository filter are unexercised.
The head-repository side of the filter compares by equality, so a boolean true would equal a repository id of 1; GitHub's data cannot produce this.
A rollback can name only a digest held by one of dev's newest 30 non-expired records; an older one is refused with the never-ran-in-dev message, which misleads but fails safe.
The previous prod digest is read in the resolve job, before the approval wait, so the summary's line can be stale if another promote finishes during the wait.
The artifact zip is read fully into memory before its single small file is checked, so a very large artifact slows or fails the resolve job.
The approved body says three jobs but lists two, and says a dev record's result is already where dev's real record says already deployed; the build follows the two jobs and dev's real value.
An actor login with a bot suffix is refused, after the role is assumed but before the document is sent, so a bot-started promote fails without deploying.
No test passes a digest input that starts with a dash; argparse refuses it with exit 2 before any call, which is safe but is not the script's own tested refusal.
